Because adjacent angles of a rhombus are supplementary, and ∠ABC=120°, ∠DAB=60°. The side length AB=AD=10, so D=(10cos60°,10sin60°)=(5,5√3), C=B+D=(15,5√3). P is the midpoint of CD, so P=((5+15)/2,5√3)=(10,5√3). Folding maps A to P, so the crease MN is the perpendicular bisector of AP. The midpoint of AP is (5,5√3/2), and the slope of AP is (5√3)/10=√3/2, so the slope of the perpendicular bisector is -2/√3. Its equation is y-5√3/2=(-2/√3)(x-5). method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/perpendicular-bisector intersection. First read the diagram as a rhombus with A,N,B along the bottom side, D,P,C along the top side, P on CD, and the fold crease MN carrying A to P. From the text take AB=10, angle ABC=120°, and P as the midpoint of CD. Put A=(0,0), B=(10,0). Since adjacent angles in a rhombus are supplementary, angle DAB=60°, so D=(5,5√3) and C=(15,5√3). Hence P, the midpoint of CD, is (10,5√3). Because folding sends A to P across MN, the crease MN is the perpendicular bisector of AP. Compute the perpendicular bisector of segment AP, then intersect it with AB, i.e. with y=0. Segment AP has midpoint (5,5√3/2) and slope √3/2, so the perpendicular bisector has slope -2/√3. Solving y-5√3/2=(-2/√3)(x-5) with y=0 gives x=35/4. Since N=(x,0), AN=35/4.
